entries.title: Choose a light or dark appearance
entries.body: Your profile page has a new Appearance setting with three choices: Light, Dark and System, which follows your device. It applies across the whole app, and it is remembered on each device separately. Until you choose, the app stays dark, so nothing changes unless you want it to.

entries.title: Look up an article's authors
entries.body: Point at an author's name at the top of an article and the card that appears has a "Find out more" line, with a Google Scholar search for that author and a web search for their name and affiliation. Each opens in a new tab. The same links sit beside each author on the article's Metadata page, which is where to find them on a phone.

entries.title: Earlier feedback shows the page it came from
entries.body: In the feedback dialog, each report on the Earlier tab says which page you sent it from. Only the page is shown, never anything you searched for, so you can tell your reports apart at a glance.

entries.title: The tag box is easier to use
entries.body: The box for adding a tag, in your library and on an article's Metadata page, is announced as "Add a tag" to screen readers, and phone keyboards that support it show a Done key. Pressing Enter still adds the tag and leaves the box open for the next one.

entries.title: Help no longer calls the typefaces experimental
entries.body: The Help page still described giving each voice its own typeface as an experiment, although it is on for every reader. Help now says so plainly, and the item is gone from its list of experimental features.
